title: errors inside a PL/pgSQL loop, with and without an exception block, and a batch job with and without COMMIT

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE stock (sku text PRIMARY KEY, qty int NOT NULL CHECK (qty > 0))
steps.note: a table with a rule: qty must be positive.
no exception block: the seventh insert breaks the CHECK, the error ends the DO block, and the six rows before it go with it.

error.message: new row for relation "stock" violates check constraint "stock_qty_check"

steps.sql: SELECT count(*) AS rows FROM stock

steps.note: an exception block around each insert: the bad row is rolled back to the block's start and skipped, the loop goes on.

steps.sql: SELECT count(*) AS rows FROM stock

CREATE TABLE jobs (id int PRIMARY KEY, archived boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false);
INSERT INTO jobs (id) SELECT g FROM generate_series(1, 5000) AS g
steps.note: a batch job: 5,000 orders to archive, one of which (3,500) is broken.
a procedure that works in batches of 1,000, with no COMMIT.
it fails in the fourth batch, and the whole CALL is one transaction: everything rolls back.

steps.sql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE archived) AS archived FROM jobs

steps.note: the same procedure with a COMMIT after every batch.
it fails in the same place. but the first three batches were committed as they finished, so they stay done.

steps.sql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE archived) AS archived FROM jobs
